description:
FOUND s491a (Opus) while measuring the #1846 arrow set character by character.
PRE-EXISTING on main 337f6a23; #1846 did not change it (deliberately -- the
`$#` family is its own arm, `_scan_array_index`).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s491a/probes/p1846-values.pl row v8):

  no strict; no warnings;
  our @ar = ("A0","A1","A2");
  print "L:$#ar->[0]\n";      # perl 5.40.3: "L:"      PCL: "L:2->[0]"

perl takes the arrow after `$#ar` (= 2) and dereferences the NUMBER as a
symbolic array name -- @{"2"}, empty, element 0 undef -- so the text is empty.
PCL's InterpScan `_scan_array_index` deliberately attaches no chain, because a
BARE subscript after `$#name` is a perl SYNTAX ERROR (`"$#{$r}[0]"`,
`"$#$r[0]"` -- the arm's own comment records the probe).  The arrow is a
different question and has the opposite answer, exactly as for the punctuation
names in #1846.

WHY IT IS LEFT: the value perl produces is a symbolic dereference of a NUMBER,
so the whole shape is nonsense that happens to parse; there is no idiom behind
it.  The #1846 runtime half (a number in container position is a symbolic ref,
%p-symref-name) means PCL would now produce perl's "" if the scanner took the
chain, so the fix is ONE call in _scan_array_index plus its guard row -- cheap,
but it changes emission for a shape nobody writes, and it was not worth a
second emission bar in that batch.

FIX SHAPE: in Pl/InterpScan.pm `_scan_array_index`, call `_scan_chain` when
`_arrow_next($text, $ev)` (the predicate #1846 added), for all four of its
returns.  Probe the BARE forms again first -- they must stay literal.
Guard: Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t's #1846 section.
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): an explicit ARROW after `$#name` inside a dq string stays literal -- `"$#ar->[0]"` is "2->[0]" in PCL and "" in perl (perl takes the chain and symbolically dereferences the INDEX); the `$#` family is the one interpolated shape the #1846 arrow rule does not cover
